title: Does lifetime learning strengthen every social action, rewarded or not?
question: In Experiments E and G, learning raised attacks ~11x and sharing ~2x, and the gift-reward loop explained only ~22% of the sharing rise. Is this a non-specific effect of the learning rule: reward reaching the input weights of every action population that was active, not just the executed one?
background: Each action population has its own plastic sensory input with potentiation-only eligibility (a_minus = 0), and a global RPE is applied to all of them. Non-executed populations that spiked still collect eligibility, so they are strengthened whenever the RPE is positive. Signalling has a cost and no reward pathway, so a reward-specific learner should not increase it. Intervention: credit_chosen_only applies the RPE only to the executed action's input weights. Seeds 200-207 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Learning raises signalling, an action with only a cost
Under learning, input weights to social actions grow more over a lifetime than those to locomotion
Crediting only the executed action lowers the attack rate
Crediting only the executed action lowers sharing given a neighbour in reach
Crediting only the executed action lowers signalling
Replication of E/G: learning raises the attack rate
